pages.title: FIRST DECISION: SAFETY
pages.body:
Alert others and arrange an emergency assistance call.

Only consider an extinguisher if you are trained,
the fire is small, the equipment is suitable,
and a clear escape route remains behind you.

If smoke, heat or a growing fire makes this unsafe,
leave by a safe route instead of attempting suppression.

Evacuating without using an extinguisher is valid.
Knowing PASS does not mean every fire can be tackled.
pages.narration: First decision: safety. Alert others and arrange an emergency assistance call. Only consider an extinguisher if you are trained, the fire is small, the equipment is suitable, and a clear escape route remains behind you. If smoke, heat or a growing fire makes this unsafe, leave by a safe route instead of attempting suppression. Evacuating without using an extinguisher is valid. Knowing PASS does not mean every fire can be tackled.

pages.title: PASS: FOUR STEPS
pages.body:
P / PULL
Remove the safety pin before squeezing.

A / AIM
Point low at the burning material, at the fire's base.

S / SQUEEZE
Press the operating lever to discharge the agent.

S / SWEEP
Move the nozzle from side to side across the base.

Keep your escape route clear. If the fire grows
or conditions become unsafe, stop and withdraw.
Follow the cylinder's instructions and training.
pages.narration: PASS has four steps. P: Pull the safety pin before squeezing. A: Aim low at the burning material, at the base of the fire. S: Squeeze the operating lever to discharge the agent. S: Sweep the nozzle from side to side across the base. Keep your escape route clear. If the fire grows or conditions become unsafe, stop and withdraw. Follow the cylinder's instructions and training.

pages.title: ORDINARY COMBUSTIBLES
pages.body:
Examples: paper, wood, cloth and office waste.
Recognize the burning material, not only flame colour.

Use an extinguisher whose label covers that material.
Water may suit ordinary solid combustibles,
but not when live electrical equipment is involved.

Never assume that all nearby materials are the same.
If you cannot identify the hazard or suitable equipment,
withdraw and request assistance.

This simulation's wastebasket incident represents
a small ordinary-combustible fire.
pages.narration: Ordinary combustible fires involve materials such as paper, wood, cloth and office waste. Recognize the burning material, not only the flame colour. Use an extinguisher whose label covers that material. Water may suit ordinary solid combustibles, but not when live electrical equipment is involved. Never assume all nearby materials are the same. If you cannot identify the hazard or suitable equipment, withdraw and request assistance. The simulation's wastebasket represents a small ordinary combustible fire.

pages.title: ENERGIZED ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT
pages.body:
Examples: a live electrical enclosure or powered device.
Treat it as energized unless authorized staff confirm
that the supply has been safely isolated.

Do not pour ordinary water onto live equipment.
It creates an electric-shock hazard.

Only trained users should consider an extinguisher
labelled suitable for this electrical hazard,
and only with safe conditions and an escape route.

Do not approach burning equipment to unplug it.
Keep clear, alert others and request assistance.
pages.narration: Energized electrical equipment includes a live enclosure or powered device. Treat it as energized unless authorized staff confirm safe isolation. Do not pour ordinary water onto live equipment: it creates an electric shock hazard. Only trained users should consider an extinguisher labelled suitable for this electrical hazard, and only with safe conditions and an escape route. Do not approach burning equipment to unplug it. Keep clear, alert others and request assistance.

pages.title: FLAMMABLE LIQUID SPILL
pages.body:
Examples include burning fuel or solvent spills.

Do not throw water onto the burning liquid.
It can spread the fuel and enlarge the fire.
Do not handle or move a burning container.

Only consider equipment labelled for the liquid,
with appropriate training and a clear escape route.
Do not improvise an agent from nearby supplies.

If the spill is spreading, smoke is building,
or safe escape is threatened, withdraw and raise help.
pages.narration: A flammable liquid fire can involve a burning fuel or solvent spill. Do not throw water onto the burning liquid: it can spread the fuel and enlarge the fire. Do not handle or move a burning container. Only consider equipment labelled for the liquid, with appropriate training and a clear escape route. Do not improvise an agent from nearby supplies. If the spill is spreading, smoke is building, or safe escape is threatened, withdraw and raise help.

pages.title: EVACUATION AND A BLOCKED STAIR
pages.body:
Use a safe stair route; do not use the lift during fire.
Close doors behind you where safe.
Once outside, go to the assembly point and stay out.

Do not enter a stair filled with fire or dense smoke.
This department model has only one staircase.
If there is no safe exit route, retreat away from danger,
close yourself in a suitable room and call for assistance.
Give your floor, room and the conditions you can observe.
Follow emergency responders' instructions.

Waiting for help is not a completed rescue.
The real department's emergency plan takes priority.
pages.narration: Use a safe stair route, not the lift, during a fire. Close doors behind you where safe. Once outside, go to the assembly point and stay out. Do not enter a stair filled with fire or dense smoke. This department model has only one staircase. If there is no safe exit route, retreat away from danger, close yourself in a suitable room and call for assistance. Give your floor, room and the conditions you observe. Follow emergency responders' instructions. Waiting for help is not a completed rescue. The real department's emergency plan takes priority.

pages.title: APPLY IT IN THIS SIMULATION
pages.body:
ALARM: red FIRE ALARM panel / white PRESS button.
ASSISTANCE: EMERGENCY CALL panel or office phone.
PC: aim and press E. VR: right ray and right trigger.

EXTINGUISHER
PC: G grab, P pin, hold left mouse and sweep your aim.
VR: right grip grab, left trigger pin, right trigger spray.
Move the right-hand nozzle to aim and sweep.

One standard cylinder is represented. Its real agent
and rating still need checking: never infer suitability
from the cylinder's colour or this prototype alone.

The practice check teaches; the assessment has no hints.
pages.narration: Apply the theory in this simulation. The red Fire Alarm panel has a white Press button. The Emergency Call panel or office phone requests simulated assistance. On PC, aim and press E. In VR, aim the right controller ray and press the right trigger. For the extinguisher on PC, G grabs, P removes the pin, and holding left mouse sprays while you sweep your aim. In VR, right grip grabs, left trigger removes the pin, and right trigger sprays. Move the right hand nozzle to aim and sweep. The installed cylinder's actual agent and rating still need verification. Never infer suitability from colour or the prototype alone. The practice check teaches; the assessment has no hints.

questions.prompt: During PASS, where should you aim?
questions.explanation:
Aim at the base, where the material is burning.
Then squeeze and sweep across that area.
Aiming at flame tips misses the burning source.
questions.narration: During PASS, where should you aim? Flame tips, the fire base, or the nearest wall?

questions.prompt: How should you treat ordinary water near live equipment?
questions.explanation:
Ordinary water can conduct electricity. Keep clear
of energized equipment and do not pour water on it.
Any extinguisher must be suitable for the hazard.
questions.narration: How should you treat ordinary water near live electrical equipment? Use a bucket, move closer, or do not use water?

questions.prompt: The only stair is full of fire or dense smoke. What now?
questions.explanation:
Do not force through the unsafe stair or use the lift.
If no safe route exists, retreat to a suitable room,
close the door and request help with your location.
questions.narration: The only stair is full of fire or dense smoke. What now? Use the lift, force through, or retreat and call for help?

questions.prompt: When should an extinguisher attempt stop?
questions.explanation:
Stop if heat, smoke, fire growth or loss of safe escape
makes the attempt unsafe. Prioritize leaving safely.
Do not wait until the cylinder is empty.
questions.narration: When should an extinguisher attempt stop? If safety worsens, only when empty, or only when told?
